newsitem.title: USA: Myriad launches cancer genes test.
newsitem.headline: Myriad launches cancer genes test.

text.p: Myriad Genetics Inc said on Thursday it would start accepting samples next week for its comprehensive BRCA1 and BRCA2 sequence analysis for susceptibility to breast and ovarian cancer.
Myriad said it will begin receiving samples on October 30 for the system, named BRACAnalysis, through its genetic testing facility, Myriad Genetic Laboratories.
The fee for the genetic analysis is $2,400, it said.
Once a gene mutation has been identified, at-risk family members are offered an analysis for that specific mutation for $395.
BRCA1 and BRCA2 gene mutations are responsible for about 90 percent of all early-onset hereditary breast and ovarian cancers, the company said.
If a woman who has had breast cancer has one of these mutations, her risk of developing a second cancer is greatly increased.
